key_insight: This paper argues for a more direct, differentiable way to code 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes from multiple views, instead of generating a full 3D representation first and compressing it later. The goal is to make feed-forward 3D reconstruction simpler, more efficient, and better suited for learning-based optimization.
problem_solved: It addresses the inefficiency and complexity of existing feed-forward 3DGS pipelines that use a "generate-then-compress" design. These methods often require separate codecs for geometry and appearance, and may rely on non-differentiable steps that limit end-to-end training.
method: Uses multi-view feature coding to represent scene information directly from sparse input images.
Replaces separate geometry/appearance compression with a more unified feed-forward encoding pipeline.
Aims to keep the reconstruction-and-coding process differentiable end-to-end for easier learning and better integration.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could simplify 3D scene reconstruction pipelines and reduce engineering overhead in codec design. It also points toward faster, more scalable 3D perception systems that can learn directly from sparse multi-view inputs.

paper_title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_authors: Seungmi Choi, Ji-Hyoun Choi, Suhyun Jo, Tae-Gwon Park, Hui Yong Kim
